heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Czech Republic
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to EOR & PEO in Czech Republic
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for EOR & PEO in Czech Republic.

steps.title: Contract Drafting & Legal Review
steps.description: Preparation of employment contracts in Czech and English. Contracts must comply with the Czech Labor Code (Act No. 262/2006 Coll.), specifically regarding notice periods, working hours (typically 40 hours/week), and mandatory vacation (minimum 4 weeks).

steps.title: Document Collection & Verification
steps.description: Collection of employee personal data, proof of qualifications, and medical fitness certificates. For foreign employees, this includes verifying work permits or employee cards (Zaměstnanecká karta).

steps.title: Social Security & Health Insurance Registration
steps.description: Mandatory registration of the employee with the Czech Social Security Administration (ČSSZ) and the relevant health insurance company (VZP, OZP, etc.) within 8 calendar days of the start date.

steps.title: Workplace Safety (BOZP) Training
steps.description: Provision of mandatory Occupational Health and Safety (BOZP) and Fire Protection (PO) training. This must be documented and signed by the employee before they commence work.

steps.title: Payroll Setup & Bank Details
steps.description: Configuring the employee in the payroll system, ensuring accurate tax ID (rodné číslo) and bank account details for monthly salary payments in CZK.

rows.label: Social Security (Employer)
values: Covers pension, sickness, and unemployment policy

rows.label: Health Insurance (Employer)
values: Paid to the employee's chosen health insurer

rows.label: Accident Insurance
values: Mandatory statutory insurance based on industry risk

rows.label: Management Fee
values: Monthly fee per employee for EOR services

items.title: Notice Period Rigidity
items.text: Statutory notice periods are a minimum of 2 months and must start from the first day of the month following the notice. Summary dismissal is extremely difficult and requires proof of gross misconduct.

items.title: Vacation Entitlement
items.text: While the statutory minimum is 4 weeks (20 days), most professional EOR employees expect 5 weeks (25 days) as a standard benefit in the Czech market.

items.title: Meal Vouchers (Stravenky)
items.text: Providing tax-optimised meal vouchers or a meal allowance (stravenkový paušál) is a highly valued and standard benefit for Czech employees.

items.title: Probation Period
items.text: Maximum 3 months for standard employees and 6 months for management roles. It cannot be extended once agreed upon.

items.title: Data Boxes (Datové schránky)
items.text: Mandatory for all legal entities. Official government communication is delivered ONLY here. Missing a message can have severe legal consequences.

items.title: Language Requirements
items.text: While international companies work in English, all official documents submitted to Czech authorities must be in Czech or accompanied by a certified translation.

items.title: Workplace Safety (BOZP)
items.text: Mandatory training is required for all employees. Non-compliance can lead to massive fines in case of workplace accidents.

faqs.question: Can I hire a contractor instead of using an EOR?
faqs.answer: Yes, but be cautious of 'Švarcsystém' (misclassification of employees as contractors). If a contractor works exclusively for one client using their equipment and following their direct orders, authorities may reclassify it as illegal employment with heavy fines.

faqs.question: What is the 13th month salary tradition?
faqs.answer: There is no legal requirement for a 13th-month salary in the Czech Republic, but it is common in some industrial sectors or as a performance-based Christmas bonus.

faqs.question: Does the EOR handle work permits?
faqs.answer: Yes, most EOR providers in Czech Republic assist with the 'Employee Card' process, which acts as both a residence and work permit for non-EU citizens.

steps.title: Data Input & Variable Pay
steps.description: Collection of variable data including overtime, bonuses, sick leave certificates (e-Neschopenka), and vacation days by the 25th of each month.

steps.title: Gross-to-Net Calculation
steps.description: Calculating gross salary, deducting 11.6% for employee social/health insurance, and applying the 15%/23% progressive income tax rates.

steps.title: Statutory Reporting
steps.description: Submission of monthly 'Overview of Payroll' to the Social Security Administration (ČSSZ) and Health Insurance companies by the 20th of the following month.

steps.title: Payment Distribution
steps.description: Transferring net salaries to employees and statutory payments to the tax office (Finanční úřad) and insurance funds, typically by the 10th-15th of the following month.

items.title: Sickness Insurance Change 2024/2025
items.text: Since 2024, employees must contribute 0.6% to sickness insurance (previously 0%). Ensure your payroll software is updated to reflect this change.

items.title: Annual Tax Reconciliation
items.text: Employees can request an 'Annual Tax Equalization' (Roční zúčtování daně) from their employer by February 15th for the previous year's taxes.

items.title: DPP vs DPČ
items.text: Work Performance Agreements (DPP) are exempt from social/health insurance if monthly income is ≤ CZK 10,000 (changing to 25% of average wage in 2025). Agreements on Work Activity (DPČ) have a lower threshold of CZK 4,000.

faqs.question: What is the current average wage used for tax ceilings?
faqs.answer: For 2025, the estimated average wage is approximately CZK 46,000 per month, which impacts the thresholds for the 23% tax bracket and social security ceilings.

faqs.question: Are bonuses taxed differently?
faqs.answer: No, all monetary bonuses are treated as regular income and are subject to the same income tax and social/health insurance contributions.

faqs.question: What is the deadline for monthly social security payments?
faqs.answer: Payments for both employer and employee contributions must reach the ČSSZ account by the 20th day of the following month.

items.title: Employer Total Cost
items.text: The total cost (Super-gross) is approximately 133.8% of the gross salary (24.8% social + 9% health).

items.title: Taxpayer Discount (2025)
items.text: Every employee is entitled to a monthly tax discount of CZK 2,570, which is deducted directly from the calculated income tax.

items.title: Progressive Tax Threshold
items.text: The 15% rate applies up to 3x the average monthly wage (approx. CZK 139,671). Income above this is taxed at 23%.

items.name: Social Security
items.description: Includes pension insurance and sickness insurance.

items.name: Health Insurance
items.description: Mandatory for all residents/employees in CZ.

items.name: Income Tax
items.description: Calculated after social/health deductions and applying tax credits.

steps.title: Determine Gross Salary
steps.description: Base salary plus any taxable bonuses or benefits-in-kind.

steps.title: Calculate Statutory Contributions
steps.description: Deduct 7.1% for social and 4.5% for health from the gross salary.

steps.title: Apply Tax Brackets & Credits
steps.description: Apply 15%/23% tax on the gross amount, then subtract the CZK 2,570 taxpayer discount and other eligible credits (e.g., children).

faqs.question: What is the maximum assessment base for social security?
faqs.answer: In 2025, the annual cap for social security is approx. CZK 2,350,416. No social security is paid on income above this.

faqs.question: Is there a cap for health insurance?
faqs.answer: No. Health insurance is calculated on the full gross amount without any upper limit.

faqs.question: How do tax-free benefits affect the calculation?
faqs.answer: Benefits like meal vouchers (up to limits) or health-related benefits (up to approx. CZK 46k/year) reduce the taxable base, increasing the net pay.

heroData.title: Incorporation in Czech Republic
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Incorporation in Czech Republic
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Incorporation in Czech Republic.

steps.title: Notarial Deed (Founding Document)
steps.description: Execution of a Memorandum of Association or Foundation Deed before a Czech notary. Requirements include company name, registered office address, and scope of business.

steps.title: Registered Office & Legal Address
steps.description: Obtaining a lease agreement and owner's consent for the registered office. Often businesses use virtual offices in Prague or Brno for the initial setup.

steps.title: Trade License (Živnostenský list)
steps.description: Registration at the Trade Licensing Office (Živnostenský úřad) for the intended business activities. Free trades are registered immediately; regulated trades require proof of qualification.

steps.title: Capital Deposit
steps.description: Opening a temporary bank account for capital deposit. The minimum capital for an s.r.o. is CZK 1, though CZK 10,000+ is recommended for credibility.

steps.title: Commercial Register Entry
steps.description: Registration in the Commercial Register (Obchodní rejstřík) via the local court or directly by the notary (quicker). The company legally exists once registered.

steps.title: Tax Registration
steps.description: Registration with the Tax Office (Finanční úřad) for corporate income tax within 15 days of incorporation.

rows.label: Trade License Fee
values: Standard fee for any number of trades

items.title: s.r.o. (Limited Liability)
items.text: Most popular for SMEs. Requires 1+ founder, CZK 1 minimum capital, and 1+ managing director. Liability is limited to unpaid capital contributions.

items.title: a.s. (Joint Stock)
items.text: Suitable for large enterprises or those planning to go public. Requires CZK 2,000,000 minimum capital and a two-tier management structure (Board + Supervisory Board).

items.title: Branch Office (Odštěpný závod)
items.text: Not a separate legal entity. The parent company is fully liable for the branch's obligations. Requires registration and a local branch manager.

items.title: Data Box (Datová schránka)
items.text: Every legal entity in CZ is automatically assigned a Data Box for official communication with authorities. Checking it regularly is mandatory.

items.title: Beneficial Owner Registry
items.text: Since 2021, companies must register their Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBO) in a central registry to comply with AML laws.

items.title: Account Overdraft
items.text: When choosing a bank for capital deposit, consider their fees for foreign currency accounts and ease of use for international transfers.

faqs.question: How long does it take to register a company?
faqs.answer: Usually 1-2 weeks. Using a notary for direct registration into the Commercial Register can shorten the process to 3-5 business days if all documents are ready.

faqs.question: Do I need a local director?
faqs.answer: No, a director can be a foreign national from any country. EU/EEA residents have an easier registration process, but non-EU residents can also be directors (requires a clean criminal record).

faqs.question: Can I use a virtual office for company registration?
faqs.answer: Yes, virtual offices are widely used and legally acceptable in the Czech Republic, especially in Prague, provided the owner's consent is verified.

heroData.title: Staffing in Czech Republic
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Staffing in Czech Republic
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Staffing in Czech Republic.

items.title: Low Unemployment
items.text: The Czech Republic consistently maintains the lowest unemployment rate in the EU (around 2.5-3.5%), leading to a highly competitive 'war for talent' especially in technical roles.

items.title: IT Hubs
items.text: Prague and Brno are major European tech hubs. Brno specifically is known as the 'Czech Silicon Valley' with a high density of software engineering talent.

items.title: Language Barrier
items.text: While English proficiency is high in IT and MNCs, local recruitment for administrative or sales roles usually requires fluent Czech (and often German in manufacturing).

steps.title: Job Specification & Localization
steps.description: Defining the role and localizing the job description to match Czech market salary expectations and benefits. Typical perks include 5 weeks vacation and 'Stravenky'.

steps.title: Sourcing & Multi-Channel Posting
steps.description: Posting on major portals like Jobs.cz, Prace.cz, and LinkedIn. For niche technical roles, active sourcing via tech communities is essential.

steps.title: Screening & Background Checks
steps.description: Reviewing CVs and conducting initial interviews. Background checks (verification of education and criminal record) are common for senior roles.

steps.title: Offer Negotiation
steps.description: Extending offers with a clear breakdown of gross salary vs net, and detailing non-monetary benefits like multisport cards or flexible working hours.

rows.label: Agency Recruitment Fee
values: Of the candidate's annual gross salary

rows.label: Job Portal Posting
values: Per listing on Jobs.cz or similar

faqs.question: What are the most popular job portals in the Czech Republic?
faqs.answer: Jobs.cz and Prace.cz are the dominant local portals. LinkedIn is very strong for professional and international roles. StartupJobs.cz is popular for the tech startup scene.

faqs.question: How long is the standard notice period for employees?
faqs.answer: 2 months is the statutory minimum, but some specialized roles might have contractual agreements for 3 months. This impacts 'time-to-join' for new hires.

faqs.question: Are 'Multisport Cards' common in Czech benefits?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Multisport card is one of the most popular non-monetary benefits, giving employees access to gyms and sports facilities across the country.

items.title: University Education
items.text: Czech candidates often place a high value on academic titles (e.g., Ing., Mgr., Bc.), which are still commonly used in formal business settings.

items.title: Reference Checks
items.text: Local references are highly valued. Czech managers tend to trust direct feedback from previous local employers more than generic recommendation letters.

items.title: Bridge Days
items.text: When a public holiday falls on a Tuesday or Thursday, many employees take the Monday or Friday off as a 'bridge day'. Recruitment processes may slow down significantly.

heroData.title: HRIS in Czech Republic
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to HRIS in Czech Republic
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for HRIS in Czech Republic.

items.title: Payroll Integration
items.text: Any HRIS used in the Czech Republic must integrate seamlessly with local payroll engines to handle 'rodné číslo' (Birth Numbers) and specific Czech tax credits.

items.title: GDPR Compliance
items.text: The system must support the 'right to be forgotten' and provide secure storage for employee medical fitness certificates, which are mandatory under Czech law.

items.title: Self-Service Portals
items.text: Czech employees highly value mobile-friendly self-service portals for requesting vacation time and viewing monthly pay slips (výplatní páska).

steps.title: Local Compliance Audit
steps.description: Mapping data fields to ensure compliance with Act No. 110/2019 Coll. on Personal Data Processing. Ensuring birth number (rodné číslo) handling is secure.

steps.title: Payroll Connector Setup
steps.description: Configuring API or file-based exports to local payroll providers (e.g., Vema or Elanor) to automate monthly variable data transfers.

steps.title: Employee Training (Czech/English)
steps.description: Training staff on how to use the system for attendance tracking, benefits management, and document signatures.

steps.title: Go-Live & Support
steps.description: Phased rollout with localized support desk to handle queries related to Czech-specific leave types (e.g., Care for a Family Member).

faqs.question: Are digital signatures legally binding for employment contracts?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided they comply with the eIDAS regulation. However, many Czech labor offices still recommend hard copies for specific termination documents.

faqs.question: Can the HRIS track 'Sickness Leave' automatically?
faqs.answer: Yes, advanced localized systems integrate with the ČSSZ 'e-Neschopenka' portal to pull sick leave data directly into the system.

faqs.question: Does HRIS help with BOZP training records?
faqs.answer: Yes, a good localized HRIS will track expiration dates for mandatory safety (BOZP) and fire (PO) training and notify managers before they lapse.

items.title: Cloud vs On-Premise
items.text: While global cloud solutions are popular, some highly regulated industries in CZ still prefer local on-premise solutions for strict data sovereignty.

items.title: Support Language
items.text: Having local, Czech-speaking support for your HRIS is a significant advantage when dealing with complex local labor law interpretations.

items.title: Integration Costs
items.text: Building a custom API connector for a local Czech payroll system can be expensive. Always check if the HRIS has pre-built connectors for Vema or Elanor.

heroData.title: Accounting in Czech Republic
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Accounting in Czech Republic
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Accounting in Czech Republic.

items.title: Double-Entry Requirement
items.text: All legal entities in the Czech Republic must use double-entry accounting (podvojné účetnictví) as per the Act on Accounting No. 563/1991 Coll.

items.title: Archiving Documents
items.text: Accounting records must be archived for 5-10 years. Invoices and tax documents must be kept for 10 years for VAT purposes.

items.title: Currency Reporting
items.text: While you can keep books in EUR/USD for management, statutory reports must be in CZK unless the company meets functional currency criteria (new in 2024).

steps.title: Document Collection (DPH focus)
steps.description: Collecting all purchase and sales invoices. Ensuring they meet the formal requirements for VAT (DPH) deduction.

steps.title: Bank Reconciliation
steps.description: Reconciling CZK and foreign currency bank statements. Managing exchange rate differences (realized and unrealized).

steps.title: VAT (DPH) Filing
steps.description: Preparing the VAT return, Control Statement (Kontrolní hlášení), and EC Sales List by the 25th of the following month.

steps.title: Financial Reporting
steps.description: Generation of monthly P&L and Balance Sheets for management review.

faqs.question: When is the deadline for the annual financial statements?
faqs.answer: Statements must be filed with the Commercial Register within 12 months from the balance sheet date, but usually coincide with the tax return deadline (March/July).

faqs.question: What is a 'Statutory Audit' threshold?
faqs.answer: Companies must be audited if they exceed 2 of these limits in 2 consecutive years: Turnover > CZK 80m, Assets > CZK 40m, Employees > 50.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for late filing of financial statements?
faqs.answer: Fines can reach up to 3% of the total assets value, although usually, the register issues a warning first for smaller entities.

items.title: Fiscal Year
items.text: The standard fiscal year is the calendar year. Changing to a different fiscal year requires notification to the Financial Office 3 months in advance.

items.title: Digital Invoicing
items.text: Electronic invoices are fully recognized, provided their authenticity and integrity can be proven. Many companies use PDF with electronic signatures.

items.title: Cash Transactions
items.text: There is a strict limit on cash payments of CZK 270,000 per day. Any amount above this must be paid via bank transfer.

items.title: AML Regulations
items.text: Anti-Money Laundering (AML) checks are mandatory for all 'obliged entities', including banks, lawyers, and now many B2B service providers. Heavy fines for non-compliance.

items.title: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO)
items.text: Failure to register UBOs in the Evidence of Beneficial Owners can lead to the inability to pay out dividends or exercise voting rights.

items.title: GDPR (Act 110/2019)
items.text: The Czech Republic has strict local interpretations of GDPR, especially regarding employee monitoring and video surveillance in the workplace.

steps.title: Labor Law Health Check
steps.description: Annual review of employment contracts, internal regulations (Vnitřní předpis), and working time records.

steps.title: Data Privacy Impact Assessment (DPIA)
steps.description: Evaluating risks related to personal data processing, particularly for HR and marketing departments.

steps.title: AML/KYC Review
steps.description: Updating 'Know Your Customer' documentation and verifying client identities against global sanction lists.

steps.title: OHS (BOZP) Workplace Audit
steps.description: Physical inspection of workplaces to ensure compliance with health and safety standards.

items.title: Whistleblowing Act 2023
items.text: Companies with 50+ employees MUST have an internal reporting system for whistleblowers. This is a critical new compliance requirement.

items.title: Electronic Identification
items.text: Czech 'Bank Identity' (BankID) is widely used for secure login to government portals, simplifying compliance for directors.

items.title: Data Box (Datová schránka)
items.text: Mandatory for all legal entities. Official government communication is delivered ONLY here. Missing a message can have severe legal consequences.

faqs.question: What happens if I don't register my company's UBO?
faqs.answer: A fine of up to CZK 500,000 can be imposed. More importantly, the company cannot pay out any profit shares or exercise voting rights until corrected.

faqs.question: Is an AML officer required for all companies?
faqs.answer: No, only for companies defined as 'obliged entities' under the AML Act (e.g., financial institutions, real estate agents, accountants).

faqs.question: Are workplace health and safety (BOZP) audits mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, every employer in the Czech Republic must ensure BOZP compliance, regardless of size. This includes regular risk assessments and employee training.

rows.label: VAT (Reduced)
values: Consolidated rate for food, pharama, books

steps.title: VAT Return (DPH)
steps.description: Submission and payment by the 25th day of the month following the taxable period.

steps.title: Corporate Income Tax Return
steps.description: Standard deadline is April 1st (printed) or May 1st (electronic). Extended to July 1st if using a certified tax advisor.

steps.title: Road Tax (Silniční daň)
steps.description: Annual filing by January 31st for vehicles used for business (only trucks > 3.5 tons since 2022).

steps.title: Real Estate Tax
steps.description: Filing by January 31st if any property was acquired or changed in the previous year.

items.title: R&D Tax Incentives
items.text: Companies can deduct up to 100% of R&D costs from their tax base. This is a significant incentive for software and manufacturing firms in CZ.

items.title: Transfer Pricing
items.text: Transactions between related parties must be at 'arm's length'. Authorities are increasingly auditing transfer pricing documentation for international groups.

items.title: Energy Tax
items.text: Specific excise duties apply to electricity, gas, and solid fuels, with exemptions available for specific energy-intensive manufacturing processes.

faqs.question: What is the threshold for VAT registration?
faqs.answer: Mandatory registration for entities with a turnover exceeding CZK 2,000,000 in 12 consecutive months (increased from 1m in 2023).

faqs.question: Can I claim back VAT on business travel?
faqs.answer: Yes, VAT on accommodation, taxi, and meal costs incurred for business purposes is generally deductible if proper tax documents are provided.

faqs.question: Is interest income subject to withholding tax?
faqs.answer: Yes, a 15% withholding tax generally applies to interest income paid to individuals, while for corporations it is often part of their regular tax base.

items.title: Tax Residency
items.text: Individuals are considered Czech tax residents if they stay in the country for 183+ days in a calendar year or have a permanent home here.

items.title: Double Tax Treaties
items.text: The Czech Republic has a wide network of over 80 double tax treaties (DTTs), which can significantly reduce withholding taxes on dividends and royalties.

items.title: Control Statement (Kontrolní hlášení)
items.text: This is a detailed VAT filing that must be submitted monthly. It's a high-focus area for tax audits due to the automation the tax office uses to spot discrepancies.

heroData.title: MSA & Legal in Czech Republic
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to MSA & Legal in Czech Republic
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for MSA & Legal in Czech Republic.

items.title: Civil Code (Act 89/2012)
items.text: The primary legal source for contracts. It offers significant freedom of contract, but mandatory provisions (e.g., consumer protection) cannot be waived.

items.title: Governing Law & Jurisdiction
items.text: While international parties can choose foreign law, Czech courts are often preferred for local real estate or employment-related disputes for enforceability.

items.title: Electronic Signatures
items.text: Recognized under the eIDAS Regulation. Higher-level signatures (Qualified) are required for specific corporate acts or government filings.

steps.title: Drafting & Review
steps.description: Preparing the MSA or local service agreement. It is standard to include detailed SLAs and liability caps (typically limited to the contract value).

steps.title: Technical & Legal Due Diligence
steps.description: Verifying the counterparty's authorization in the Commercial Register and checking for existing litigations/insolvencies.

steps.title: Signing Ceremony / Digital Execution
steps.description: Execution via platform (DocuSign) or physical signing with certified signatures (Czech POINT) if required for the Commercial Register.

items.title: IP Ownership
items.text: Under Czech law, 'works for hire' automatically grant the employer economic rights, but moral rights remain with the author. Contracts must explicitly address this transfer.

items.title: NDA Enforcement
items.text: Czech courts recognize contractual penalties for NDA breaches, but they must not be 'disproportionately high' or they may be reduced by a judge.

items.title: Representative Action Act 2024
items.text: New legislation allows class-action style lawsuits for consumer and data protection breaches, increasing risk for B2C companies.

faqs.question: Can I use an English-only contract in the Czech Republic?
faqs.answer: Yes for B2B. However, for the Commercial Register or labor contracts, a Czech translation is highly recommended and sometimes mandatory.

faqs.question: What is 'Czech POINT'?
faqs.answer: A government-run service (often at post offices) where you can get documents certified, extracts from registers, or convert electronic documents to paper.

faqs.question: Are oral contracts valid in CZ?
faqs.answer: Generally yes for simple transactions, but the Civil Code requires written form for various acts, including real estate transfers and most corporate changes.

heroData.title: Software in Czech Republic
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Software in Czech Republic
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Software in Czech Republic.

items.title: Engineering Talent Pool
items.text: The Czech Republic has over 150,000 IT specialists. Prague and Brno (the 'Czech Silicon Valley') are the primary hubs for high-end engineering.

items.title: Tech Stack Popularity
items.text: Java, C#, and React/Node.js dominate. There is also a strong niche in cybersecurity (Avast/Gen) and automotive software (Škoda/VW Group).

items.title: R&D Maturity
items.text: Many global firms (Microsoft, Oracle, Red Hat) have their core engineering centers in CZ due to the high mathematical and logical skill level.

sections.title: Setting Up a Dev Hub in CZ

steps.title: Location Strategy
steps.description: Choose between Prague (highest talent volume, higher costs) or Brno (academic center, strong IoT/Embedded focus).

steps.title: Recruitment & Salary Benchmarking
steps.description: Competition is fierce. Standard benefits include flexible hours, 5 weeks of vacation, and 'bridge' days.

steps.title: Infrastructure & SecOps Setup
steps.description: Establishing secure VPNs and local office infrastructure. CZ has excellent fiber connectivity (up to 10Gbps in hubs).

items.title: Technical Debt & Quality
items.text: Czech engineers are known for high quality 'clean code' but can be more conservative/critical during planning phases compared to US counterparts.

items.title: University Partnerships
items.text: The CTU (Prague) and BUT (Brno) are world-class. Partnering for thesis projects is a common 'long-game' recruitment strategy.

items.title: Tax on Stock Options
items.text: Historically complex in CZ. While new laws are improving ESOP taxation, it's still less straightforward than in the UK or US.

faqs.question: Are English-speaking teams common in CZ?
faqs.answer: In the IT sector, English is the default working language. Almost all specialists are fluent, especially in international hubs like Prague.

faqs.question: What is the standard notice period for developers?
faqs.answer: Usually 2 months, starting from the first day of the following month. This can make rapid scaling difficult without active pipelines.

faqs.question: Are developers usually employees or contractors?
faqs.answer: Both. High-earning seniors often prefer the 'OSVČ' (freelance) model for tax optimization, though the 'švarcsystém' (disguised employment) risks must be managed.

heroData.title: Marketing in Czech Republic
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Marketing in Czech Republic
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Marketing in Czech Republic.

items.title: Dual Search Engine Market
items.text: The Czech Republic is unique in Europe because Google (85%) competes with a strong local player, Seznam.cz (12-15%). A successful strategy MUST cover both.

items.title: Language Nuance
items.text: Czech is a highly inflected language. Standard automated translations often fail to capture correct grammar/tone. Always use native copywriters.

items.title: Social Media Trends
items.text: Facebook and Instagram remain dominant for B2C, while LinkedIn is the go-to for professional B2B services. TikTok is rapidly growing among Gen Z.

steps.title: Market & Keyword Research
steps.description: Analyzing trends on both Google Trends and Seznam Reporter to identify local search intent and seasonal patterns.

steps.title: Localization & Transcreation
steps.description: Adapting global creative assets to local cultural contexts. This includes adjusting humor, imagery, and product positioning.

steps.title: Media Buying & Optimization
steps.description: Setting up Sklik (Seznam's PPC platform) and Google Ads. Continuous monitoring and A/B testing of Czech-language copy.

items.title: Seznam.cz Ecosystem
items.text: Beyond search, Seznam operates top news portals (Novinky.cz) and map services (Mapy.cz) which are critical for local display advertising.

items.title: E-commerce aggregators
items.text: Heureka.cz and Zbozi.cz are vital for any retail business. Many Czech consumers start their product search on these comparison sites rather than on Google.

items.title: Cookie Law Compliance
items.text: The Czech Republic has strict 'opt-in' cookie requirements. Ensuring your marketing tech stack compliant with local UOOU standards is mandatory.

faqs.question: Should I focus only on Google for SEO in CZ?
faqs.answer: No. While Google has the majority, ignoring Seznam means missing up to 20% of the market, which is often less competitive and more loyal.

faqs.question: What is the average lead time for a marketing campaign?
faqs.answer: Planning to launch usually takes 4-6 weeks for integrated campaigns. PPC can be launched within 1-2 weeks.

faqs.question: How important is influencer marketing in the Czech Republic?
faqs.answer: Very. The market is compact, and local influencers (especially on Instagram and YouTube) have high trust and engagement rates among specific demographics.
